step_by_step_reasoning: The Carano Cloud microservices architecture is designed for fleet management applications. The end user interacts with a web front-end hosted on S3. User requests go to API Gateway, which decouples the client from backend microservices running on ECS (Kotlin/Vert.x) and Lambda (TypeScript). Async messaging is managed by publishing events from ECS to SNS topics (fanout), which subscribe to SQS queues for specific service types (fan-in), ensuring single-message execution by either ECS instances or Lambda functions.

graph.name: Carano Cloud Microservices Architecture
graph.notes: Carano transitioned from an on-premise JMS architecture to a cloud-native architecture using S3, API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, SNS, and SQS to achieve decoupling, technology flexibility, and reliable message handling.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: End user accessing the web application.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Hosts the web application static content.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Handles incoming API requests and decouples clients from backend microservices.

nodes.name: Lambda
nodes.notes: Serverless compute running TypeScript microservices developed with Serverless Framework.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Containerized microservices running Kotlin and Vert.x toolkit on Docker.

nodes.name: SNS
nodes.notes: Receives fanout messages from backend services.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues messages for specific service types to ensure idempotent single-instance processing.

nodes.notes: DynamoDB database component present on the architecture diagram.

edges.notes: S3 delivers the web application to the user browser.
User sends API requests to API Gateway.
API Gateway routes relevant API calls directly to Lambda functions.
API Gateway routes requests to microservices hosted on ECS.
ECS services send messages to SNS topics for fanout distribution.
SNS fans out published messages to target SQS queues.
SQS queues trigger Lambda functions for async message processing.
ECS service instances pull messages from SQS queues for single-processing fan-in.
